# nix.dev

> Official tutorials, guides, and reference documentation for the Nix ecosystem.

Nix is a package manager and build tool, Nixpkgs is a package collection and library, and NixOS is a Linux distribution configured using Nix.
Use tutorials and guides for tasks, and the component's reference manual for command syntax, functions, and configuration options.
Match the manual to the installed Nix version or the project's Nixpkgs and NixOS release; the latest release may differ from the version in use.
Check each page's prerequisites, including any experimental features required by its examples.
The links below point to the existing rendered documentation.

## Reference manuals

- [Nix manual versions](https://nix.dev/reference/nix-manual.html): Select a Nix reference manual for command syntax, the Nix language, store operations, and Nix configuration.
- [Nixpkgs manual](https://nixos.org/manual/nixpkgs/stable/): Stable-release reference for package construction, the standard build environment, language-specific build helpers, and library functions.
- [NixOS manual](https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/): Stable-release reference for installation, system configuration, services, and NixOS options.
- [Glossary](https://nix.dev/reference/glossary.html): Definitions of terms used across the Nix ecosystem.

## Getting started

- [Install Nix](https://nix.dev/install-nix.html): Installation instructions.
- [First steps](https://nix.dev/tutorials/first-steps/): Introductory lessons on working with Nix.
- [Nix language basics](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nix-language.html): An introduction to reading the Nix language.

## Development environments

- [Ad hoc shell environments](https://nix.dev/tutorials/first-steps/ad-hoc-shell-environments.html): Obtain tools temporarily and run programs using nix-shell.
- [Declarative shell environments](https://nix.dev/tutorials/first-steps/declarative-shell.html): Define a development environment in shell.nix.
- [Reproducible interpreted scripts](https://nix.dev/tutorials/first-steps/reproducible-scripts.html): Declare an interpreter and dependencies for a script.
- [Automatic environment activation](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/direnv.html): Activate a project's shell with direnv and nix-direnv.
- [Python development environment](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/python-environment.html): Create a development environment for a Python application.
- [Sharing build and shell dependencies](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/sharing-dependencies.html): Reuse package dependencies in a development shell with inputsFrom.

## Packaging and reproducibility

- [Packaging existing software](https://nix.dev/tutorials/packaging-existing-software.html): Build C/C++ software using derivations and stdenv.
- [Package parameters and overrides](https://nix.dev/tutorials/callpackage.html): Compose package recipes and customize their arguments with callPackage.
- [Working with local files](https://nix.dev/tutorials/working-with-local-files.html): Select build inputs with lib.fileset and copy source files into the Nix store.
- [Pinning Nixpkgs](https://nix.dev/tutorials/first-steps/towards-reproducibility-pinning-nixpkgs.html): Make a development environment reproducible by selecting a specific Nixpkgs revision.
- [Managing remote sources with npins](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/dependency-management.html): Pin and update the remote sources used by Nix expressions.
- [Cross compilation](https://nix.dev/tutorials/cross-compilation.html): Build software for a different host platform.

## Modules, NixOS, and deployment

- [Module system tutorial](https://nix.dev/tutorials/module-system/): Learn how modules declare options and combine configuration values.
- [Module system deep dive](https://nix.dev/tutorials/module-system/deep-dive.html): Work with option types, conditional definitions, defaults, and submodules.
- [NixOS virtual machines](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nixos/nixos-configuration-on-vm.html): Build and run a virtual machine from a NixOS configuration.
- [NixOS integration tests](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nixos/integration-testing-using-virtual-machines.html): Test system configurations and services with testers.runNixOSTest.
- [Bootable ISO images](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nixos/building-bootable-iso-image.html): Build installation media from a NixOS configuration.
- [Docker images](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nixos/building-and-running-docker-images.html): Build and run container images using Nixpkgs tooling.
- [Provisioning remote machines](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nixos/provisioning-remote-machines.html): Install and deploy NixOS over SSH with nixos-anywhere and disko.
- [Distributed builds](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nixos/distributed-builds-setup.html): Configure remote machines to perform Nix builds.

## Binary caches and continuous integration

- [Using a binary cache](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/add-binary-cache.html): Configure Nix to obtain build results from an additional binary cache.
- [Setting up an HTTP binary cache](https://nix.dev/tutorials/nixos/binary-cache-setup.html): Serve and sign build results from a NixOS machine.
- [GitHub Actions](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/continuous-integration-github-actions.html): Build and cache project environments in continuous integration.

## Concepts and troubleshooting

- [Flakes](https://nix.dev/concepts/flakes.html): Understand flake inputs and outputs, experimental status, and adoption considerations.
- [Channels and other concepts](https://nix.dev/concepts/faq.html): Understand channel branch choices, flakes, and sandbox-related questions.
- [Best practices](https://nix.dev/guides/best-practices.html): Avoid common Nix language and reproducibility pitfalls.
- [Troubleshooting](https://nix.dev/guides/troubleshooting.html): Diagnose binary cache, store database, and installation problems.
- [Practical frequently asked questions](https://nix.dev/guides/faq.html): Find guidance on formatting, non-Nix executables, and common NixOS tasks.

- [All guides](https://nix.dev/guides/): Browse recipes and task-oriented guides.

- [Post-build hooks](https://nix.dev/guides/recipes/post-build-hook.html): Upload build results to an S3-compatible cache, with implementation caveats.
- [Contributing documentation](https://nix.dev/contributing/documentation/): Find the contribution workflow and documentation style guide.
- [Sitemap](https://nix.dev/sitemap.xml): Discover additional documentation pages beyond this curated selection.
